analysis.successDefinition: `npm publish --dry-run` from packages/llm-http-proxy exits 0 with the packed tarball containing dist/, README.md (created this horizon), and LICENSE, and author set to a non-empty value; @opentelemetry/* appear only as peerDependencies marked optional via peerDependenciesMeta (never in dependencies); a Logger-compatible span exporter ships with one test proving an LlmLogEntry becomes a span when peers are installed and one test proving the exporter is inert and never imported/activated when peers are absent; no span attribute or emitted field leaks raw payload/header data (redaction invariant holds); the horizon keeps 3-5 phases (hard ceiling 7); package build/lint/typecheck/jest and root gates stay green after every phase; no interceptor request-path code changes; the recorded p99 latency miss (173.88% of baseline) is left deferred with no remediation code.
assumptions: npm registry is reachable to install the optional @opentelemetry/* peers locally — needed for the OTEL demo, not for the publish dry-run itself.

The existing Logger seam signature (entry: LlmLogEntry) => void is sufficient surface for the span exporter; if it is not, extending the seam is in-scope only as the minimal necessary change, because blockers.md line 3 is still open on exactly this question.
The binding package-identity decision (llm-http-proxy 0.2.0, MIT) stays closed; the author value is chosen without reopening that decision.
Because npm v7+ auto-installs peerDependencies, peerDependenciesMeta.optional:true is required for opt-in to genuinely be opt-in, and the current dependencies:{} stays empty.
The OTEL proof targets a minimal span via @opentelemetry/api plus an SDK package — no OTLP exporter or collector is needed to demonstrate the seam.

"Gates stay green" means the package build/lint/typecheck/jest suite (with dist rebuilt before the root consumer re-links) plus root build/jest; the RUN_BENCH-gated benchmark is not part of the default gate path.

blockers.md line 3 is unresolved: the Logger seam is entry-only with no span context or trace state, so writing the first true consumer (the span exporter) may require a seam signature extension — that must be a deliberate decision, not a quiet redefinition of the bar.

If @opentelemetry/* peers are declared without peerDependenciesMeta.optional:true, npm v7+ auto-installs them for every consumer, turning opt-in into a forced runtime dependency and violating the binding OTEL-posture decision.

The span exporter is the first real consumer of the Logger seam and could naively copy entry/request fields into span attributes, breaking the package's core redaction invariant ('no raw sensitive value in any emitted log entry or span, including error paths').

Installing the optional peers requires network/registry access and mutates the package lockfile; if the registry is unreachable, the OTEL bar cannot be proven and the horizon must re-plan (the dry-run itself needs no network).

`npm publish --dry-run` may surface publish-hygiene issues beyond the two known ones; scope discipline is required — fix only the two named gaps plus anything that actually blocks a clean dry-run, with no gold-plating (repository field, CI, badges).

The root consumer consumes the package via link:, so any package change needs a dist rebuild before the root gate goes green; an accidental runtime dep would leak OTEL into the root Nest build and turn a green root gate red.

discoveryFindings.finding: The Logger seam is exactly `export type Logger = (entry: LlmLogEntry) => void`; consoleLogger emits JSON.stringify(entry) and noopLogger is a no-op; logger.ts has zero runtime imports (only `import type { LlmLogEntry } from './options'`).

discoveryFindings.finding: logger.test.ts enforces via source-string greps that logger.ts imports no @nestjs/@angular, that the console adapter body never references req./res./getHeader, and that interceptor.ts contains no inline JSON.stringify(entry).
discoveryFindings.implication: The exporter must live in a separate new module (e.g. src/otel.ts) wired as a Logger-compatible sink; its attribute mapping must copy only entry fields, mirroring the consoleLogger no-raw/no-header invariant, or the existing seam tests (and the redaction invariant) would be violated.

discoveryFindings.finding: Redaction happens BEFORE the entry is assembled (redact.ts: DEFAULT_SENSITIVE_FIELDS ~60 substring needles, DEFAULT_PLACEHOLDER '[REDACTED]', idempotent, input never mutated); LlmLogEntry = {timestamp, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, callerTrace, url, maskedRequestBody?, maskedResponseBody?, error?} — no headers, and with capturePayloads=false (default) no body fields at all.
discoveryFindings.implication: A span exporter may safely copy url/model/inputTokens/outputTokens/callerTrace into span attributes, timestamp into span start time, and error into span status/events — the entry is already redacted, so as long as the exporter reads only entry fields it cannot leak raw payload or header data into attributes.

phases.name: Add OTEL span exporter module
phases.goal: Write src/otel.ts: a Logger-seam-compatible span exporter that lazily attaches to OpenTelemetry only when the optional peer is installed, copies only LlmLogEntry fields into the span, and is a no-op when the peer is absent; re-export it from the package's main entry so a real consumer can reach it.
phases.rationale: The package's Logger seam is just the function type `(entry: LlmLogEntry) => void`, and this exporter is its first real consumer. A top-level static import of any @opentelemetry/* package would make typecheck/lint/jest fail for anyone without the peers, so the peer is resolved at runtime via a try/catch require; and only entry fields may be copied into span attributes, preserving the package's core no-raw-data redaction invariant. The re-export from src/index.ts is what makes the demo a consumer-reachable extension interface (the package's exports map exposes only the root entry); without it a consumer could only deep-import the module. The user endorsed keeping this re-export at the alignment preview.
changes: Create src/otel.ts exporting a Logger-compatible function (e.g. `export const otelSpanLogger: Logger`) that satisfies the `(entry: LlmLogEntry) => void` seam from src/logger.ts, using only a type-only import (`import type`) of Logger/LlmLogEntry so nothing from the package's own seam becomes a runtime dependency.

Feature-detect the peer once at module load: `try { const { trace } = require('@opentelemetry/api') as typeof import('@opentelemetry/api'); ... } catch { /* peers absent → inert */ }` — never a top-level static import. Add a scoped `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` comment above the require (the recommendedTypeChecked lint config flags `require`), and cast the require result to the imported type so the no-unsafe-* lint rules do not fire on `any`.

When the peer is present, have the exported function create a span (e.g. name 'llm-http-proxy.llm-call') via `trace.getTracer('llm-http-proxy')`, set the span start time from `entry.timestamp`, copy ONLY entry fields into span attributes (model, inputTokens, outputTokens, callerTrace, url; maskedRequestBody/maskedResponseBody only when present on the entry; on `entry.error` set an error status and record the message), and end the span. Never read the request/response object or headers.
When the peer is absent, the exported function must be a no-op that never throws.
Re-export `otelSpanLogger` from src/index.ts so consumers can import it from the package root and pass it as the `logger:` option.

Run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build` — all must stay green; the dual CJS+ESM build picks up the new module with zero build-config changes (the ESM dist's bare `require` throws and is safely caught, making the ESM path inert — the acceptable safe failure mode for the demo).
inputs: src/logger.ts — `export type Logger = (entry: LlmLogEntry) => void`, the seam the exporter must implement
src/options.ts — the LlmLogEntry fields the exporter may read (timestamp, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, callerTrace, url, maskedRequestBody?, maskedResponseBody?, error?)

The redaction invariant: only entry fields may be copied into span attributes; never the request/response object or headers

phases.compensation: Revert by deleting src/otel.ts and removing the otelSpanLogger re-export from src/index.ts.

rubric.label: Exporter satisfies the Logger seam and is consumer-reachable
rubric.ruleStatement: The exported function is a plain `(entry: LlmLogEntry) => void` compatible with the existing Logger type, its only imports from the package's own modules are type-only, and it is re-exported from the package root so a consumer can import it without a deep path.
passCriteria: `src/otel.ts` declares `export const otelSpanLogger: Logger = (entry: LlmLogEntry): void => {...}` — the export is typed as the existing `Logger` and its signature is exactly `(entry: LlmLogEntry) => void`, not async and with no extra parameters.

Running `grep -n "import.*from './logger'" src/otel.ts` and `grep -n "import.*from './options'" src/otel.ts` shows only `import type` lines — no value import from the package's own seam becomes a runtime dependency.

`src/index.ts` contains `export { otelSpanLogger } from './otel';`, so `import { otelSpanLogger } from 'llm-http-proxy'` resolves from the package root (verified against the exports map in `package.json`).
failureExamples: The exported function returns a `Promise` or takes a second parameter, so it is no longer assignable to `Logger` and the interceptor's `this.logger(entry)` call site would typecheck-fail.
`src/otel.ts` value-imports `Logger`/`LlmLogEntry` from `./logger`/`./options`, adding a runtime dependency on the package's own seam.
`otelSpanLogger` is only reachable via a deep import like `llm-http-proxy/dist/esm/otel.js` because no re-export was added to `src/index.ts`.

rubric.label: Peer is runtime feature-detected, never a hard dependency
rubric.ruleStatement: OpenTelemetry stays optional: the peer is resolved lazily once at module load via a try/catch `require` — never a top-level static import — and when the peer is absent the exported function is a non-throwing no-op that never touches OTEL.
passCriteria: `grep -n "@opentelemetry" src/otel.ts` shows the peer referenced only inside a `require(...)` call or an `import type` used as a cast — there is no top-level `import ... from '@opentelemetry/api'` statement in the file.

The `require('@opentelemetry/api')` sits inside a `try { ... } catch { ... }` block, and the line immediately above it carries the literal comment `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires`.
The catch branch only records that the peer is absent (an inert-state flag or equivalent) — it contains no `throw`, no `console.error`, and no call into any OTEL API.
With `node_modules/@opentelemetry` temporarily removed (or the require forced to fail), calling `otelSpanLogger(entry)` twice returns without throwing on both calls and no span is emitted.
failureExamples: A top-level `import { trace } from '@opentelemetry/api'` at the top of `src/otel.ts` — it passes every local gate because the peer is installed, but breaks typecheck/lint/jest for any consumer without the peer.
The `require` is not wrapped in try/catch, so a missing peer throws at module load and the package can no longer be imported at all.
The catch branch logs to console or rethrows, so the package emits noise or crashes for consumers who chose not to install the optional peers.

rubric.label: Span attributes come only from LlmLogEntry fields
rubric.ruleStatement: The span's attributes are derived exclusively from the entry object's fields. The exporter never reads the request/response objects or headers, preserving the package's core no-raw-data redaction invariant.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "\.(req|res|headers|request|response)" src/otel.ts` returns no matches — the only data source is the `entry` parameter, whose fields are timestamp, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, callerTrace, url, maskedRequestBody?, maskedResponseBody?, and error?.
Every attribute key written to the span is one of the entry field names above; no attribute value comes from `JSON.stringify(entry)` or from any object other than the entry itself.
`maskedRequestBody` and `maskedResponseBody` are written to the span only behind an explicit presence check (e.g. `entry.maskedRequestBody !== undefined`) — never copied unconditionally.
On the error path the span records the error status and `entry.error.message` only; the entry is never mutated and no field outside the entry (e.g. a stack or payload) is added.
failureExamples: A span attribute such as `http.request.body` populated from the raw request body or from `req.headers`.
The exporter closes over or receives the `ClientRequest`/response object and reads `headers`, `statusCode`, or `body` from it.
`maskedRequestBody`/`maskedResponseBody` are written to attributes even when undefined, so default (non-capturing) runs emit `undefined`-valued attributes.

rubric.label: Each call yields one complete, deterministic span
rubric.ruleStatement: When the peer is present, every invocation creates exactly one span from a tracer named `llm-http-proxy`, starts it at `entry.timestamp`, ends it on every path including the error branch, and is deterministic — identical input produces identical spans with no shared module-level state.
passCriteria: `grep -n "getTracer" src/otel.ts` shows the span is obtained via `trace.getTracer('llm-http-proxy')` and `grep -n "llm-http-proxy.llm-call" src/otel.ts` shows that exact span name literal.
The span start time is set from the entry (`span.setStartTime(entry.timestamp)` or the API equivalent) before attributes are assigned — not from module-load or call time.
`span.end()` is reachable on every code path that creates a span, including the `entry.error` branch — no invocation leaves an un-ended span.

Calling `otelSpanLogger(entry)` twice with the same entry and the peer present yields two spans with identical attributes — there is no module-level counter, no incrementing sequence, and the passed entry object is not mutated.
failureExamples: The span is created via `new Span()` or with a hard-coded start time instead of `trace.getTracer('llm-http-proxy')`.
The error path returns before `span.end()`, leaking one open span per failed LLM call.
A module-level `let callCount` is baked into an attribute, so identical input produces different spans on successive calls.

rubric.label: Change is strictly additive to the declared two files
rubric.ruleStatement: This phase touches exactly two files — the new `src/otel.ts` and the re-export line in `src/index.ts`. The interceptor request path and every other source file are byte-identical to the phase-1 baseline, and no runtime dependency is added.
passCriteria: `git diff <phase-1-baseline> -- packages/llm-http-proxy/src/interceptor.ts` (or `git diff HEAD` with HEAD at the phase-1 baseline) shows zero changed lines in `src/interceptor.ts`.
`git status --short packages/llm-http-proxy/src` lists exactly the untracked `src/otel.ts` and the modified `src/index.ts` — no other `src/*.ts` file appears in the change set.
`package.json` still has `"dependencies": {}` — no runtime dependency was added (the OTEL peers remain only in `peerDependencies`/`peerDependenciesMeta` from phase 1).
failureExamples: A diff that edits `src/interceptor.ts`, e.g. threading the exporter into the emit call site at the `this.logger(entry)` line.
`@opentelemetry/api` accidentally moved into `dependencies`, force-installing it on all consumers and breaking opt-in semantics.
Unrelated edits to `src/redaction.ts` or `src/options.ts` riding along in this phase's commit.

rubric.label: Package and root gates pass with the new module in both builds
rubric.ruleStatement: The package typecheck/lint/test/build gates and the root gates all stay green, and the existing dual CJS+ESM build compiles the new module with zero build-config changes — the ESM dist's bare `require` throws inside the try/catch and is the declared inert failure mode, not a crash.
passCriteria: Running `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build` inside `packages/llm-http-proxy` exits 0 with no errors or lint findings.

After `npm run build`, both `dist/cjs/otel.js` and `dist/esm/otel.js` exist (with `.d.ts`/`.d.ts.map` siblings), and the build ran with no changes to `tsconfig.cjs.json`, `tsconfig.esm.json`, or the `build` script.

Reading `dist/esm/otel.js` shows the `require('@opentelemetry/api')` call inside the try/catch block — in the ESM build the bare `require` throws and is caught, leaving the module inert (the accepted safe failure mode).
The root workspace build and jest gates (`npm run build` and `npm test` from the repo root) also pass.
failureExamples: `npm run build` fails, or silently drops `otel` from one of the two output formats (e.g. only `dist/cjs/otel.js` is emitted).
The ESM output contains a `require('@opentelemetry/api')` outside the try/catch, so importing the ESM build without the peer installed throws at import time.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a top-level static `import ... from '@opentelemetry/api'` — it passes every local gate because the peer is installed, silently killing opt-in activation — so grep `src/otel.ts` for a bare top-level `@opentelemetry` import and move it into the try/catch `require` before running gates.

phases.name: Test span recording and peer-absent inertness
phases.goal: Prove both exporter behaviors in the default jest suite with no environment flag: an LlmLogEntry becomes a span when the OTEL peers are installed, and the exporter is inert when they are absent.
phases.rationale: The exporter is only trusted when both behaviors are verified: with the optional peers present an LlmLogEntry must become a real span, and with them absent the exporter must stay inert. Both proofs are fast (an in-memory span round-trip is milliseconds) and the OTEL packages are already devDependencies, so they belong in the always-green default `npm test` — the opt-in posture applies to runtime consumers, never to the package's own test gate.
changes: Create src/otel.test.ts (it matches the existing jest testRegex, so no jest-config change) with a 'peers present' test: register a BasicTracerProvider with an InMemorySpanExporter and SimpleSpanProcessor (all from @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base), call the exported otelSpanLogger with a sample LlmLogEntry, then assert getFinishedSpans() returns exactly one span whose attributes match the entry's fields and whose start time equals entry.timestamp (compare via the SDK's epoch-millisecond representation).
After that test, shut the provider down and reset the global tracer (provider.shutdown() plus trace.disable() from @opentelemetry/api) so no other suite is affected.

Add a 'peers absent' test: inside jest.isolateModules, call jest.doMock('@opentelemetry/api', () => { throw new Error('peer not installed'); }), re-require src/otel.ts so its load-time feature detection runs against the throwing mock, and assert calling the exported logger with an entry does not throw — proving the try/catch path is inert.

Run the default `npm test` (no RUN_OTEL or any env flag) and confirm both proofs pass; then run the full two-level gate — package `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` (rebuild dist so the root link: consumer sees the new module) and root `nest build` + root jest — and confirm all stay green, with src/interceptor.ts and both jest configs untouched.
inputs: src/otel.ts — the exported Logger-compatible span exporter from phase 2
@opentelemetry/api and @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base devDependencies (installed in phase 1) providing BasicTracerProvider, InMemorySpanExporter, SimpleSpanProcessor
The peer-absent simulation technique: jest.doMock('@opentelemetry/api', () => { throw new Error('peer not installed'); }) inside jest.isolateModules
A sample LlmLogEntry fixture covering every field the exporter maps (timestamp, model, tokens, callerTrace, url, masked bodies, error)
phases.expectedResult: src/otel.test.ts runs in the default `npm test` (no env flag) with two passing proofs — one span recorded via InMemorySpanExporter with matching attributes and start time when peers are present, and a non-throwing no-op when peers are simulated absent — and the full two-level gate (package typecheck/lint/test/build + root nest build/jest) is green.

rubric.label: An entry becomes exactly one real span
rubric.ruleStatement: With the OTEL peers installed, calling the exported Logger-seam function with one LlmLogEntry produces exactly one finished span recorded through the real SDK in-memory pipeline — not a hand-rolled fake.
passCriteria: Imports `BasicTracerProvider`, `InMemorySpanExporter`, and `SimpleSpanProcessor` from `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` and wires them together
Calls the exported `otelSpanLogger` (the Logger-compatible function from `src/otel.ts`) with a sample LlmLogEntry

rubric.label: Span content matches the entry
